description.narrative: (Pakistan): The recently launched USAID Building Healthy Families activity will expand access to and utilization of essential health care services in Pakistan, including quality family planning (FP) and maternal, newborn, and child health (MNCH) services. The activity will also include basic nutrition interventions to improve health outcomes for women of reproductive age and children under five. A focus of this activity will be to address the new challenges in FP/MNCH exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic and impacts from the historic 2022 floods in Pakistan, which have caused disruptions in health service provision, the contraceptive supply chain, and staff capacity building.. ..The activity will implement a health-systems strengthening approach, focusing on supporting interventions in areas such as policy, advocacy, human resources, leadership, and governance. The activity will also address Pakistan's high fertility and low contraceptive prevalence rates within the context of a rapidly growing population; and support the Government of Pakistan in its flood recovery efforts by improving access to essential health services, including reproductive health and family planning.. ..This IM contributes $1 million to the Maternal and Child Health (MCH) earmark and $3.5 million to the Family Planning and Reproductive Health earmark.. ...
